concepts.angle: Runners are told to lift less. The opposite is true if you sequence it.
concepts.hook: if you want to get jacked and still run, use this split

slides.text: most people run their legs into the ground, then wonder why nothing grows.
lift heavy twice. run easy three times. never on the same legs, never on the same day.
hard days hard, easy days easy. the middle is where progress goes to die.
your easy run should feel insultingly slow. that is the point of it.
one long run a week. everything else is maintenance for that one.
eight weeks of this beats eight months of doing both badly.

concepts.closerKicker: we post one of these every week

concepts.angle: Same money, opposite life. The comparison does the arguing.
concepts.hook: a $1,200 phone and a $1,200 race entry cost the same

slides.text: one of them you replace in two years and never think about again.
the other one you talk about for the rest of your life.
nobody has ever described an upgrade cycle as the hardest thing they have done.
the entry fee is not the cost. the six months before it are the cost.
that is also the entire return.

concepts.closerKicker: spend it on something that changes you

concepts.angle: VO2max work is simple and everyone overcomplicates it.
concepts.hook: six sessions that actually move your vo2max

slides.text: four by four minutes, hard, three minutes easy between. the boring one that works.
thirty by thirty. thirty seconds on, thirty off, until form breaks.
hill repeats. six times ninety seconds, walk down, no heroics on the first one.
the long tempo. forty minutes at a pace you could hold a bad conversation at.
fartlek. unstructured, by feel, once a week, when you cannot face a plan.
the time trial. once a month. it is a measurement, not a workout.

concepts.angle: The unglamorous inputs are the ones that separate people.
concepts.hook: the athletes still improving after five years do less, not more

slides.text: they protect sleep like it is a training session, because it is one.
they take the deload week even when they feel fine. especially then.
they eat the same boring four meals and stop thinking about it.
they never train through a sharp pain. dull, maybe. sharp, never.
adding is easy. subtracting is what actually moves you forward.

concepts.closerKicker: nobody posts about any of this
